findings.title: Data race on shared err and totalBatchesIndexed in errgroup goroutines
findings.body: Every worker goroutine assigns its result to the `err` variable captured from the enclosing `init` function (`_, _, err = s.build(...)`) and increments `totalBatchesIndexed` with no synchronization. With initWorkers > 1 these are data races, which this PR makes more likely by removing the global BuildIndex lock. One goroutine can return another goroutine's error, so a failure can be hidden or reported against the wrong resource, and the reported indexed count is wrong. Declare a local `err` inside each goroutine and use an atomic counter.

findings.title: Concurrent builds of the same key now race; duplicate indexes and file-dir conflicts
findings.body: Without the whole-function lock, two callers of getOrCreateIndex for the same key (concurrent Search requests, or watch events arriving while init is still building) can both miss the cache and build in parallel. For file-based indexes, both call bleve.New on the same directory, and one of them fails or corrupts it. The last writer also overwrites the other's index in the cache, leaking it and double-counting the IndexTenants and IndexedKinds metrics. A per-key lock or singleflight is needed.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates cache without lock
findings.body: TotalDocs ranges over `b.cache` without holding `cacheMu`. It is now called from init via the new log line, and other goroutines (watch handling, concurrent builds) can write the map at the same time. That is a concurrent map read/write, which can make the Go runtime throw a fatal error. Take `cacheMu.RLock()` while iterating.

findings.title: Search init now blocks constructor; Stop/cancel unavailable and ctx never cancelled on failure
findings.body: NewResourceServer now runs the full index build synchronously, so module startup blocks for the whole build, which can be long. If Init fails, the server is discarded but `cancel` is never called. The background contexts are leaked, along with any watcher or poller goroutines that were already started (for example the search watch on context.Background()).
